tests: release-verify in registry mode waits until the registry serves the version, then verifies it
release-verify in registry mode times out with NOT SERVED and exit 75 when the registry never serves the version
release-verify in registry mode fails a served but broken version at its steps without waiting out the deadline

consumesExternalOutput.program: npm cache add, npm view and npm install against the public registry, spawned by scripts/release-verify.sh
consumesExternalOutput.provenance: Both captures are real output from npm 11.18.0 on node v26.6.0, 2026-09-23, against registry.npmjs.org with a fresh cache per command; the tests' stub npm replays their exit codes and stderr rather than typed strings. rule (f)'s shell arm binds scripts/release-verify.sh because it is a *.sh that spawns npm and node. RESIDUE: the captures are of a version that is NEVER served, not of a version during its propagation window; that a propagating version answers the same way is inferred from the incident (release run 35839356656) and has not been captured during a real propagation. FIVE MEMBERS at five points of one pipeline: member 0 removes the wait (the incident); member 1 gives up after one poll; member 2 misclassifies a served version as not served; member 3 (fix round 1, Opus CR-003) drops the pause between polls, which the never-served test's upper bound on attempts reddens; member 4 (fix round 1, Opus CR-004) drops the last npm error from the NOT SERVED line.
